title: Tenant-scoped trace routing shim for legacy Jaeger clients
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: A subset of customers still run legacy Jaeger clients that emit protobuf/Thrift span payloads to our legacy ingestion endpoints. We want to migrate routing and backend selection into the new OTLP-first pipeline without requiring client upgrades.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, tenant-scoped routing shim that accepts legacy Jaeger payloads, translates them to OTLP trace format, attaches tenant metadata (API key -> tenant mapping), and forwards to the new trace broker which performs per-tenant routing to Tempo/Jaeger-compatible backends or long-term storage. The shim must enforce tenant isolation, respect sampling hints, and surface errors for opaque payloads.

Non-goals: full feature parity for all Jaeger tags, live schema migration of trace IDs, or long-term storage migration. We will not change client SDKs as part of this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Shim accepts Jaeger HTTP/UDP submissions and returns 200 for valid tenant-mapped requests
Payloads are translated to OTLP v1.0 TraceRequest and injected with tenant_id metadata
Shim enforces per-tenant rate limits derived from quota service and returns 429 when exceeded
Routing decisions are emitted as structured logs and metrics and visible in trace-routing dashboard
E2E test: sample legacy Jaeger client sends spans -> Shim -> Trace Broker -> Tempo backend; spans appear in Tempo within SLA (99th p95 < 1s for routing)
technical_notes: Language: Go (align with trace-relay and existing OTLP adapters)
Ingress: HTTP POST /api/v2/spans for Jaeger-over-HTTP and UDP thrift receiver for compatibility mode
Translation: use internal jaegerproto-to-otlp adapter library (new) to map span.timestamp, operationName, tags -> otel.attributes
Tenant mapping: validate API key header x-redwood-key and query tenant metadata service (cache TTL 30s)
Sampling: preserve Jaeger sampling flags where present and map to otel.trace_flags; if absent consult tenant sampling policy service
Rate limiting: token-bucket per-tenant enforced in shim before forwarding
Observability: emit otlp metrics (incoming_rate, translate_errors, forward_latency_ms, dropped_spans), structured logs for routing decisions
Failure modes: on translation error, return 400 and increment translate_errors metric; on broker unavailability, buffer to local disk (bounded 100MB) and retry with backoff up to 60s
Security: validate and sanitize tags to avoid header-injection; ensure TLS for all egress to trace broker; KMS usage for API key encryption at rest
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy shim as a small fleet in us-east-1 behind existing legacy ingress. 2) Enable tenant mapping for non-critical tenants (canary group ~5% by traffic). 3) Monitor metrics for translation errors and forward latency for 48h. 4) Expand to 25%, 50% then 100% after stability gates. 5) Decommission legacy ingestion after full migration and customer communication.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: translation may drop non-standard Jaeger tags -> Mitigation: keep raw-jaeger blob in otel.attributes._legacy_blob for forensic retrieval
Risk: high-throughput spikes could overflow buffer -> Mitigation: implement backpressure headers and circuit-breaker to fail fast for noisy tenants
Risk: cross-tenant leakage of tags -> Mitigation: strict tenant_id injection and validation; unit tests for metadata enforcement
testing_plan: Unit tests for jaeger->otlp translation covering common tag types and baggage
Integration tests with trace-broker in staging verifying routing to tempo and jaeger backends
Chaos test: simulate broker flapping and assert buffering+retry behavior
Performance benchmark: sustain 10k spans/sec with 1MB average payload under 50ms translate latency
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ravi Patel: Created ticket and initial spec. Marked as P1 due to several customers on legacy SDKs.

2025-02-18 - Ava Chen: Spike complete. Prototype UDP receiver and translation library demonstrate <20ms median translation time. Noted tag collisions for 'user' vs 'user_id' — adding normalization rules.
2025-02-24 - Security review requested. Security team called out need for explicit tag sanitization and encryption-at-rest for API keys.
2025-02-28 - QA: Integration tests with trace-broker staging show intermittent 503s during broker leader elections; adding local buffering and exponential backoff.
2025-03-02 - PM review (Sofia Martinez): Approved canary plan. Please add observability dashboards for per-tenant throttles before canary start.
